M/vNAK BIIAVAN, Q BAUADUK SHAH ZAIAK MARC, 
NIW DELHI 110002 



IS I 4327.1967 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

ELECTRIC FANS AND REGULATORS 

FOR USE IN SHIPS 

0. FOREWORD 

Otl This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 26 October 1967, after the draft finalized by the Electric Fans Sectional 
Committee had been approved by the Electrotcchnical Division Council. 

0.2 Electrical equipment, such as fans, in a ship have generally to 
function under more arduous conditions than on land. There are, however, 
many common aspects between fans for domestic purposes and those used 
in ships. This standard has been drawn up specially to cover the require- 
ments and methods of testing of electric fans and regulators for use in 
ships. Both ceiling type and cabin type fans are covered in this speci- 
fication, 

0.3 While preparing this specification the work going on this subject in the 
corresponding I EC Committee has been kept in mind and assistance has 
also been derived from the International Recommendation on this subject. 

0.4 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standard specifications on 
electric fans. Other specifications published so far in the scries are: 

IS : 374-1966 Electric ceiling type fans and regulators {second revision) 

IS : 555-1967 Electric table type fans and regulators {second revision) 

IS : 1169-1967 Electric pedestal type fans and regulators {first revision) 

IS : 1709-1960 Fixed capacitors for fans 

IS : 2312-1967 Propeller type ac ventilating fans {first revision) 

IS : 2997-1964 Air circulator type electric fans and regulators 

IS : 3588-1966 Electric axial flow fans 

IS : 3963-1966 Roof extractor units 

IS : 4283-1967 Hot air fan 

0.5 This standard contains clauses which call for agreement between the 
purchaser and the supplier and which require the manufacturer to supply 
certain technical information at the time of placing orders. The relevant 
clauses are 6.4.1, 6.7, 15.1, 17.3 and 18.1 {see also Appendices A and B). 



IS I 4327.1967 

0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement ,of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing 
the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2:1960*. 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded oflf value should be 
the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



1, SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies the requirements and methods of tests for 
electric motor operated propeller fans of the cabin and ceiling type and 
their associated regulators for use on single-phase ac and dc circuits not 
exceeding 250 volts, intendefi for air circulation in living spaces in ships, 

1.2 This standard does not cover fans used for air intake and exhaust. 

1.3 This standard also does not apply to fans for use in hazardous locations 
where it may be necessary to have flameproof enclosures {see IS : 2148-1962t). 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply. 

2J Cabin Type Fan — A propeller-bladcd fan, having two or moise 
blades, directly driven by an electric motor, and intended lor use with frde 
inlet and outlet. It may be a table fan or bracket-mounted fan for bulkhead 
or deckhead mounting. , 

2.2 Ceiling Type Fan — A propeller-bladcd fan, having two or moi^e 
blades, driven by an electric motor and provided with a device for suspensicHi 
from the ceiling of a room so that the blades rotate in a horizontal plane. 

2*3 Rating — A statement of the operating characteristics assigned to the 
fan by the manufacturer when tested in accordance with 18. 

2.4 Rated Voltage — The voltage assigned to the fan by the manufacturer 
and marked on it. 

23 Rated Voltage Range — The voltage limit assigned to the fan by the 

manufacturer and marked on it. 

2«6 Rated Frequency — In the case of ac fans, the frequency assigned 
to the fan by the manufacturer and marked on it. 

2^7 Rated Frei|uency Range — In the case of ac fans, the limits of 
frequency assigned to the fan by the manufacturer and marked on it. 

•Rules for rounding off nummcal values (revised), 
tSpedfioitioix for flameproof cnclojwrcs of electrical apparatus. 



IS : 4327-1967 

2.8 Rated Speed — The rotational speed specified by the manufacturer 
at which the fan develops the specified output at the rated frequency or 
frequency range and rated voltage or voltage range, if ac motor operated. 

2.9 Rated Input — The input assigned to the fan by the manufacturer and 
marked on it. 

2.10 Cooling Air Temperature — The temperature of the surrounding 
atmosphere in which the fan operates. 

2.11 Service Value — The air delivery in cubic metres per minute divided 
by electrical power input to the fan in watts at the voltage (and frequency, 
if ac) specified for the test. 

Note — For a cabin type fan fitted with an oscillating mechanism, the electrical input 
in watts is measured with the fan under normal full speed rx)ndition», that is, with 
oscillating mechanism in action, whereas the air delivery is determined with the oscillating 
mechanism out of action. 

2.12 Blade Sweep — The diameter of the circle traced out by the extreme 
tips of the fan blades. 

2.13 SixeofFau — The blade sweep in millimetres, 

2.14 Plane of Fan Blades — The middle plane of the solid of revolution 
traced out by the fan blades. 

2.15 Plane of Anemometer Vanes — The middle plane of the solid 
of revolution traced out by the vanes of the anemometer. 

2.16 Test Plane — The plane containing the plane of the anemometer 
vanes. This is the horizontal plane in the rase of a ceiling type fan, and the 
vertical plane in the case of the cabin type fan. 

2.17 Types of Enclosures of Motors and Regulators 

2.17.1 Totally Enclosed Type — An enclosure which prevents circulation 
of air between the inside and outside of the case, but not necessarily air-tight. 

2.17.2 Ventilated Type — An enclosure in which the ventilation is not 
materially obstructed while the live parts are protected mechanically against 
accidental or careless contact, 

2*18 Mounting ~ The mounting of a fan is the means of attaching the fan 
system (motor and blades) into the required position. 

2.19 Caamping Device — A means by which any positioning device, that 
is, swivel, trunnion, oscillating mechanism, etc, may be held in the desired 
position. 

2.20 Insulation 

2.20.1 Double Insulation — Denotes insulation comprising both functional 
insulation and supplementary insulation. 



IS I 4327- 1967 

2*20.2 Functional Insulation — Denotes insulation necessary for the proper 
functioning of equipment and for basic protection against electric shock. 

2.20.3 Supplementary Insulation {Protective Insulation) — Denotes an indepen- 
dent insulation provided in addition to the functional insulation in order 
to ensure protection against electric shock in case of failure of the functional 
insulation. 

2.20.4 Reinforced Insulation — Denotes an improved functional insulation 
with such mechanical and electrical qualities that it provides the same 
degree of protection against electric shock as double insulation. 

2*21 Twe Tests — Tests carried out to prove conformity with the require- 
ments of this standard. These are intended to prove general qualities and 
design of a given type of fan. 

2*22 Routine Tests — Testt carried out on each fan to check the essential 
requirements which are likely to vary during production. 

2.23 Acceptance Tests — f ests carried out on samples selected from a lot 
for the purpose of verifying th^ acceptability of the lot. 

2.23.1 Lot — All fans of the same type, grade, category and ratings 
manufactured by the same factory during the same period^ using the samq 
process and materials. 

3. SIZES, SPEEDS AND TYPES 

3.1 The standard sizes of ceiling type fans shall be : 

600, 750, 900, 1 050 and 1 500 nmi 

3.2 The standard sizes of cabin type fans of oscillating or non-oscillating 
types shall be : 

250, 300 and 400 nun 
Note — Sizes of hm specified in 3.1 and 3*2 arc subject to a tolerance ot ±b mm. 

3.3 The peripheral speed of any size of ceiling type fan shall not exceed 

1 200 m/min at the highest value of the rated voltage range and (if ac) at 
the highest rated frequency. 

3.4 The peripheral speed of any size of cabin type fan shall not exceed 

2 150 m/min at the highest value of the rated voltage range and (if ac) 
at the highest rated frequency. 

4. RATED VOLTAGE 

4.1 The preferred rated voltages for fans shall be 220 and 230 V dc or 230 
and 240 V [see IS : 585 - 1962*) single-phase ac at 50 c/s or 1 15 V, single- 
phase ac at 60 c/s. 

♦Recommended voltages and frequency for ac transmission and distribution systems {rtvised), 

5 



18 t 4327.1967 

5. RATED FREQjUENCY 

5«1 The rated frequency shall be the standard frequency of 50 c/s for ac 
fan motors. 

Note — Nevertheless, fans with motors made for other frequencies shall be considered 
to comply with the specification provided they do so in all relevant respects, 

6. DESIGN AND GENERAL CONSTRUCTION 
6,1 Eadosures 

64.1 Motors and regulators for both cabin type and ceiling type fans 
shall be either of the ventilated or totally enclosed type. 

6*1,2 The enclosures of all-insulated fans may form part or whole of the 
supplementary or reinforced insulation. 

6*2 Stampiiigs — Stampings of fan motors shall be made from electrical 
steel sheet {see 648 - 1962*, IS : 649 - 1963t and IS : 3024 - 1965J). 

6*3 Blades — Fans shall be fitted with two or more well-balanced blades 
made from metal or other suitable material. The blades and blade carriers 
shall be securely fixed so that they do not loosen in operation. 

6*4 Guard 

6.4.1 Except in the case of cabin type fans with flexible blades, guards 
shall be supplied, and shall be regarded as part of the fan construction. 
Guards for ceiling type fans shall not be regarded as integral parts of the 
fan, and if required shall be specified by the customer at the time of placing 
the order or enquiry. 

6.4.2 Fans of the cabin type or ceiling type (other than those with flexible 
blades) if fitted with guards, shall have a suitable robust guard either of the 
open or closed mesh type to provide, in normal use, adequate protection 
against personal injury as far as possible. If a close mesh guard is provided, 
the nominal diameter of the wires of the guard shall be not less than 1 *60 mm 
and the centre distance between the wires shall not exceed 10 mm* 
Non-oscillating cabin fans shall have a handle or other means, on the front 
of the guard to permit directional adjustment without risk of fingers pene- 
trating the guard itself. 

6.5 Heat Resistance — No readily flammable material shall be used in 
the construction of fan and regulator. Moulded parts, if used, shall be of 
such materials as will withstand the maximum temperature attained in the 
adjacent component parts. 



^Spedfication for f teel aheeu for magnetic circuito of power electrical apparatus (non- 
oriented steel) {nvited)^ 
tMe^Kxis <H testing steel sheets for magnetic circuits of power electrical apparatus (rmsid), 
^Spedficatton for electrical steel sheets (oriented). 



ISt 4327.1967 

6.6 Moisture Resistance — Only suitable material which is rcsbtant to 
moisture shall be used. The speed regulator shall be capable of with- 
standing the moistureproofness test specified in 18.5. 

6.7 Bearings — Instructions for the proper lubrication of bearings shall 
be furnished by the manufacturer. Proper types of bearings should be used 
to ensure a reasonably silent operation. 

6.8 Supply Cord — As an alternative to terminals or contacts for fixed 
connection, fans may be fitted with a flexible lead suitably connected to the 
terminals for connecting to the supply. This lead shall have a minimum 
length of 4-5 metres of tough rubber, PVC or equivalent insulated and 
sheathed [see IS : 434 (Part I) - 1964* and IS : 434 (Part II) - 1964t, 
IS : 694 (Part I) - 1964J and IS : 694 (Part II) - 1964§]. For fans intended 
to be earthed, a 3- or 4-c<)re cable shall be supplied with the earthed core 
connected to the earthing terminal or contact provided on the body of the 
fan; a 3-core cable being used, except in the case of a split-field dc fan in 
which case a 4-core cable would be required. 

For fans with double or Reinforced insulation, a 2-core cable shall be used, 
except in the case of a split-field dc fan in which case a 3-core cable would 
be required. 

NoTB — When intematkitial agreement is reached on the colour identification of the 
earthing core, the appropriate colours shall be used. 

6.9 Cord Grip — All fans fitted with supply cord shall be provided with 
a cord grip such that the conductors are protected from strain including 
twisting and abrasion, and capable of passing the tests specified in 18.6. 

The cord grip shall preferably be of insulating material or, if of metal^ be 
adequately insulated. 

On fans with double or reinforced insulation, the cord grip shall be so 
designed that the flexible cord does not come into contact with the fixing 
screws if they arc accessible, or in contact with accessible metal parts. The 
cord grip shall be suitable for the different types of cords which may be 
attached to the fan. 

6*10 Protective Measures — From the point of view of protection against 
electric shock, electric fans shall be of either of the following two types: 

a) With functional insulation only — with the accessible metal parts 
designed to be connected to an earthing terminal or contact; and 

b) With double or reinforced insulation — with the accessible metal 
parts not designed to be connected to an earthing terminal or contact.

fSpecification for rubber-insulated cables: Part II With aluminium conductors (revised).

€•10.1 All fans and regulators with functional insulation only shall be 
provided with an earthing terminal or contact, which shall be indelibly 
marked with the symbol '^\ The earthing terminal or contact shall 
not be used for any other purpose. 

641 Fr^iimctiiom Agmiiuit Direct Conttmct — In the assembled fan and 
regulator, live parts shall not be accessible to the standard test finger (sei 
IS : 146^1 - 1959*). In the case of a double insulated fan, both functionally 
insulated parts and live parts shall not be accessible to the standard test 
finger. 

6.12 M«tliocl of Movntfaig 

6.12.1 Ceiling Typi Fan — The mounting system of a ceiling type fan shall 
comprise a cradle or backplate integral with or capable of being rigidly 
fixed to the fan motor. Means shall be provided to enable the backplate 
or cradle to be securely attached to the deckhead. 

6.12 J! Cabin Type Fan — The mounting system of a cabin type fan shall 
comprise a bracket or pedestal having means for secure attachment to table 
or bulkhead or deckhead. The mounting of cabin type fans may be one 
of the following types: 

a) Rigid — The direction of draught is changed only by changing the 
position of the fan. 

b) Semi-rigid — A trunnion and/or swivel arrangement incorporated in 
the mounting so that the direction of the draught may be altered to 
suit the requirements. 

c) Oscillating — Suitable device is provided by which the direction of 
the axis of the draught is changed automatically and continuously 
in one plane. 

d) Double-oscillating or gyrostatic — Suitable device is provided by 
which the direction of the axis of the draught is changed 
automatically and continuously in more than one plane. 

6.12.2.1 Clamping devices — All clamping devices, where provided, shall 
be of strong simple design. They shall be so arranged that the mechanism 
may be positively adjusted without there being undue risk of their working 
loose. 

6.13 Gaiwcitors — Capacitors, if any, shall be easily replaceable and 
placed at sufficient distance from the windings, so that its maximum safe 
working temperature is not exceeded. Capacitors shall be clearly marked 
with the maximum safe working temperature, and the corresponding voltage 
and capacitance. Capacitors shall comply with IS : 1709 - 1960t.

7. FINISH 

7.1 All the surfaces of both (an motor with blades and regulator, if any, 
shall be of corrosion resisting material or shall be suitably and durably 
protected against corrosion. 

8. INSULATING MATERIALS 

8.1 With the exception of resistance wires in regulators, the windings of fans 
and re^lators shall be insulated either with Glass A» Class B or with Class E 
insulatmg materials which comply with limits of temperature-rise specified 
in 18.4 and moistureproofness test (for regulators only) specified in 18.5. 
These insulating materials are detailed in IS : 1271 - 1958*. 

9. SPEED REGULATION 

9.1 Cabin tyj)e and ceiling type fans may be provided as single speed models 
without speed regulators. 

9*2 Both dc cabin and dc ceiling type fans may be provided only with a 
split field winding to enable two ruruiing speeds to be obtained by means 
of a 2-way and *Off ' switch. This switch may be attached to the fan ajid 
considered a part of the c<mstruction. Alternatively, it may be separattly 
mounted in which case it shall not be considered as part of the fan, and if 
required should be specified on the order or enquiry. 

10. SPEED REGULATORS 

10.1 Regulators may be either built-in or a separate unit. 

10.2 Regulators shall be capable of reducing the speed of the fan by mini- 
mum percentage of the full speed shown in the following table, at the voltage 
(and frequency, if ac) specined for the test: 

ac and dc Ceiling dc Cabin Type ac Cabin Type ac Cabin Type 
Type Fans Fans Shaded-PoU Capacitor Fans 

Fans 

50 percent 40 percent 20 percent 50 percent 

Fans shall be capable of running continuously on any of the contacts of 
the regulator at the rated voltage or voltages {see 2.4) or within the whole 
rated voltage range {see 2.5) whichever is applicable. 

10.3 Where regulators are provided for ceiling type fans, they shall give a 
minimum of 5 running speeds and an 'Off' position. 

10.4 Where regulators are provided for cabin type fans, they shall give a 
minimum of 2 running speeds and an *Off ' position. 

*Cl||jHiilication of insulating materials for ciectrical machinery and apparatus in relation 
to their thermal stability in service. 



IS t 4327-19C7 

10.5 The regulator shall have an *Off ' position preferably next to the lowest 
speed contact, and shall be provided with the necessary number of running 
positions, with the speed steps equal as fiair as possible. 

10.6 Where a regulator is provided with a capacitor not permanently 
connected across the motor terminals, provision snail be made so that the 
capacitor is discharged when the regulator is in the 'OfT position. 

10.7 The regulator handle or knob or push buttons shall either be of in* 
sulating material or, if of metad, shall be adequately insulated electrically and 
thermally so that its temperature-rise above ambient is limited to 20''C. All 
metallic parts associated vnth it shall be protected from accidental contact. 

10.8 The rejgulator handle or knob shall be so placed that it may be safely 
and conveniently manipulated and unless continuously variable, shall only 
rest in one of the regulating positions. The handle or knob shall be so 
designed that it does not become loose in use. The running and *Off * 
positions of the regulator shall be distinctly and clearly marked and the 
indicator on the operating handle or knob shall correctly indicate the 
position of the regulator. 

10.9 The regulators shall have mechanical stops for the regulator moving 
contact to prevent accidental contact with the metallic body of the regulator 
in the event of forced overtravel of the knob. 

10.10 The mechanism of the regulator shall be so designed as to ensure 
positive contact at each running position. In the case of inductance type 
regulator, it is essential that no portion of the inductive winding may remain 
permanently short-circuited in any of the running positions. 

11. STARTING 

11.1 Ceiling type fans shall be capable of starting up from rest with the 
regulator, if any, at the lowest speed step when 85 percent of the rated 
voltage or 85 percent of the lowest voltage in the voltage range is applied. 

11.2 Cabin type fans shall be capable of storting up from rest with the 
regulator at the lowest speed step when 85 percent of the rated voltage or 
85 percent of the lowest voltage in the voltoge range is applied with the 
oscillating mechanism in action and in the worst position, in the case of fan 
of oscillating and double oscillating fans and with the axis about which the 
fan motor swivels being at an an^e of 45^ to the horizontol plane so that 
the air is directed outwards. 

12. mTERGHANGEABlLrrY 

12.1 The motor of the fen of a particular size and model and its associated 
regulator and set of blades shall be interchangeable such that the performance 
of the fan keeps within limits of standard. 

10 



ISt 4327- 19S7 

13. SILENT OPERATION 

13.1 Precautions shall be taken in the manufacture of fans and regulators 
to ensure a reasonable degree of silence at all speeds. 

14. OSCaiXATING MECHANISM OF CABIN TYPE FANS 

14JI The number of oscillations (that is, complete to-and-fro movement) 
per minute at full speed shall be not less than four. 

I4i2 Whether or not the ang^ular movement of the mechanism is variable, 
an angular movement of not less than 60^ shall be available {see Fig. 1). 




Fig. 1 AnouIar Movement of Oscillation 

IAJ5 A device shall be provided to render the oscillating mechanism in- 
operative when desired. The method of operating the device shoutid 
preferably be indicated. Means shall be provided to ensure that when 
properly installed, the fan is not stalled or overturned if the oscillating 
mechanism is impeded. 

15. RADIO INTERFERENCE 

15*1 Fans shall be fitted with a radio interference suppressor, if necessary, 
to give a reasonable degree of suppression. The purchaser should specify 
his requirements at the time of enquiry or order. 

16. COMMUTATION 

16.1 Motors with commuutors shall have a fixed brush setting. They 
shall work from full speed to lowest speed without undue sparking and 
without injury to the surface of commutator or brushes. Carbon brushes 
and brush holders shall comply according to the relevant Indian Standards. 

17. MARKING 

17.1 Each Ian shall be indelibly marked with at least the following in- 
formation: 

a) Manufacturer's name, trade name of fan (if any) and number; 

b) Rated voltagc(s) or voltage range; 

c) Type of fan, ac or dc; 

U 



IS : 4327 - 1967 

d) Frequency or frequency range of powci supply, if of <ic; 

e) Input in watts; 

f) Size of fan; 

g) Number and type of blades; 

h) Size and grade of brushes; and 
j) Country of manufacture. 

Nori, — Tiic trade name, vohagc and iizc of ihc fan^ bliall b(* inaikctl on the associated 
regulator. 

17«2 In the case of a fan provided with an earthing terminal or contact, 
it shall be indelibly marked with the symbol 'i\ 

17.3 For additional information that the manufactmer may be rec^uestcd 
to supply, see Appendix A. 

17.3.1 The fans may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 

17#3%2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made 
thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of 
Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained 
from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



18. TESTS 

18.1 General — Tests shall be classified as type, acceptance and routine 
tests. Acceptance test, if requested, shall be made on samples selected 
according to a method of sampling agreed to between the purchaser and 
the manufacturer. A recommended method of sampling is given in 
Appendix B. Type tests shall be carried out on three samples.

18.1.2 Limits of Error of Electrical Instruments — The error in the indicated 
value of ammeters, voltmeters and wattmeters shall not exceed 0*5 percent 
of full scale value for instruments used for type tests. For routine and 
acceptance tests, industrial class instruments [see 18:1248-1958^) may be 
used. 

18.1»3 Test Voltage — The voltage at which the tests are conducted shall 
be as follows. 

18.1.3.1 When a rated voltage is indicated on the name-plate, the test 
shall be conducted at the rated voltage. If the fan is specified for two or 
more distinct rated voltages with three or more supply terminals, the tests 
shall be carried out at the voltage corresponding to the most unfavourable 
connection. For this purpose the slower speed of a split field dc fan aiiall 
be regarded as a regulated speed.

18«2«1 Tfst Chamber — The fan shall be tested in a test chamber measur-

be covered except for a centrally situated circular opening (top opening), 
the diameter of which shall be greater than the blade sweep of the fan by 
not more than 20 percent and not less than 10 percent. The central 
diaphragm in which the top of)ening is located shall be not more than 
6 mm thick.

Fio. 3 Ran of Test Chamber and Screen 

(, 

IBJldJt The outer chamber shall be provided at a uniform di^J^cc 
of 1 to 1-25 m laterally round the test chamber and reaching froiji the 
ground-ievei to a height of not less than 3 m. One or more walls of a room 
may be utilized as sides of the outer chamber provided they comply with 
all the necessary conditions. 

UL2.1.3 The observer shall take readings from a position between the 
chamber and the outer chamber and a small shelf for electrical instruinents 
may be provided in this space. Except for these, the space between the 
chamber and the outer chamber and the space inside the test chamber 
shall be clear of all obstructions, and there shall be no heating or cooling 
apparatus anywhere in the test chamber which is likely to interfere with the 
test results. 

18.2.1.4 The room in which the test chamber and the outer chamber 
are erected shall be reasonably free from extraneous draughts while the 
test is being carried out. 

18.2.2 Height of Fan --The fan shall be placed at such a height that the 
plane of the fan blades is 3 m from the ground-level and lies in the plane 
of the top edge of the diaphragm containing the top opening in the roof of 
the test chamber. 

18.2.3 Any ceiling external to the test chamber or any projecting beam 
which might interfere with the air flow shall be not less than one metre above 
the top opening, that is, not less than 4 m from the ground-level at thkt 
point. 



15 



IS t 4327-1967 

18.2.4 Testing Instruments — The air movement shall be measured by 
means of a rotating vane anemometer having an internal diameter not 
exceeding 100 mm. It is recommended that the anemometer be calibrated 
frequently. 

18.2.5 Arrangement of Apparatus — The arrangement of the apparatus shall 
be such as to permit the anemometer being moved in either direction along 
both diagonals of the test chamber in a test plane 1 -50 m below the plane 
of the fan blades. The anemometer shall be supported in such a manner 
as to offer as little obstruction as possible to the air flow. 

18.2.6 Procedure for Test 

18.2.6.1 Before taking any steps towards testing a fan in accordance 
with thb standard, it is essential that it should have been *run-in' to steady 
conditions. A period of two hours is considered adequate for this purpose. 

18.2.6.2 The measurements shall be carried out with the fan running 
at full speed at the test voltage. 

18.2.6.3 Readings shall be taken along each of the four semi-diagonals 
of the test chamber commencing at a point 40 mm from the vertical axis of 
the fan motor by increments of 80 mm so that each reading represents an 
air velocity at the mean radius of an annulus 80 mm wide. The readings 
shall be continued until the true air velocity falls below 9-0 metres per 
minute. 

18*2.6.4 Each reading shall consist of the time taken by an air move- 
ment of 300 m measured by the anemometer, except when such air move- 
ment takes more than two minutes; the reading shall then consist of the 
time taken by a movement of some convenient and readable quantity of 
air requiring approximately two minutes. 

18.2.6.5 The average air velocity over any annulus shall be the mean 
of the readings on either side of the axis of the fan blades at each mean 
radius of annulus. 

18.2.6.6 The average velocity so obtained, multiplied by the area of 
the corresponding annulus shall be taken as the total air delivery through 
that annulus. 

18.2.6.7 The sum of the air deliveries through all such annuli up to the 
limit of readings mentioned in 18.2.6.3 shall be taken as the measured air 
delivery of the fan for the purposes of this specification. 

18.2.7 Air conditions (temperature, relative humidity, pressure) obtained 
at the test chamber during tests shall be recorded with the test result. 

Note — No correction ii to be made until an agreement it available on correction 
factor. 

183 Air Delivery of Cmbiii Type Fane (Ty|ie Teet) 

19.3*1 Test Chamber — The fan shall be tested in a test chamber 

16 



IS : 4327-1967 

measuring 4-5 X 4-5x3-0 m high which shall be reasonably free from 
extraneous draughts while the test is being carried out. 

18.3J.1 The test chamber shall be free from obstruction other than the 
stand on which the fan is mounted. Any table or shelf for electrical instru- 
ments shall be on the intake side of the fan, beyond a distance of 0*90 m 
from the plane of the fan blades. No heating or cooling apparatus shall be 
used in the test room while the test is in progress. 

18.3.1.2 The fan shall be mounted with the blade centre 1 -20 m from the 
floor and with the front of blades at least 1-20 m from the back wall and 
at least 1-80 m from the side walls and the wall in front. 

18.3.2 The air movement shall be measured by means of medium or 
low velocity rotating vane anemometer having an internal diameter of 
70 mm suitable for the range of velocity to be measured. Revolving vane 
anemometers having a diameter up to 100 mm may also be used alternatively. 
It is reconuncnded that the anemometer be calibrated frequently. 

18.3.3 Arrangement of Apjfiaratus 

I8«3.3.1 The arrangerdient of the apparatus (see Fig. 4) shall be such as 
to permit the anemometer being moved in a horizontal plane containing tjie 
axis of the fan, the movement being at right angles to the axis and extendable 
in both directions. The aoemomcter shall be supported in such a manner 
as to offer as little obstruction as possible to the air flow. The axis of the 
anemometer vane shall always be parallel to the axis of the fan blades.

18,3*3.2 The distance between the test plane and the plane of the fan 
blades shall be three times the blades sweep in millimetre. For example, 
for a 250-mm fan, the distance between the test plane and the plane of 
the fan blades shall be (3x250) or 750 mm. 

18.3.4 Procedure for Test 

18.3.4.1 Before taking any steps towards testing a fan in accordance with 
this standard, it is essential that it should have been 'run-in' for at least 
one houF at the highest voltage of the rated voltage range. 

18.3.4.2 The measurements shall be carried out with the fan running 
at full speed at the test voltage and with the guard in position. 

18.3.4.3 Readings shall be commenced at a point 20 mm from the axis 
of the fan blades, and shall progress along the horizontal line in each direction 
by increments of 40 mm wide. Readings shall be continued in each 
direction until the true air velocity falls below 24 metres per minute. 

18.3.4.4 Each reading shall consist of the time taken by an air move- 
ment of 300 m measured by the anemometer, except when such air move- 
ment takes more than 2 minutes; the readings shall then consist of the time 
taken by a movement of some convenient and readable Quantity of air 
requiring approximately two minutes. In no case should tne duration of 
the reading be less than one minute. 

18.3.4.5 The average air velocity over the annulus shall be the mean 
of the readings on either side of the axis of the fan blades at each mean 
radius of annulus. 

18.3.4.6 The average velocity so obtained, multiplied by the area of 
the corresponding annulus shall be taken as the total air delivery through 
that annulus. 

18*3.4.7 The sum of the air deliveries through all such annuli up to 
the limit of readings {see 18«3*4*3) shall be taken as the measured air delivery 
of the fan for the purposes of this standard. 

18^*5 Air conditions ^temperature, relative humidity, pressure) obtained 
at the test chamber dunng tests shall be recorded with the test result. 

NoTB — No correcUon is to be made until an agreement is available on correction 
factor.

18.5 Moistnreproofness Test (for Regulators Only) (Type Test) 

18.5.1 The regualtor shall be subjected to and shall satisfy the tests 
specified in 18.10 and 18.11 immediately after having been placed for a 
period of 24 hours without current being passed through the motor and 
regulator, in a closed receptacle in which relative humidity is maintained at 
90 to 95 percent at any temperature chosen in the range of 40"" to 50°C. 
Whatever temperature is chosen for this test, it shall be maintained constant 
to within ±1 dcg. 

18.6 Cord Grip Test (Type Test) — The flexible cord shall be connected 
to the fan with the cord grip in the normal position. The conductors shall 
be introduced into the terminal and screws, if any, shall be slightly tightened 
so that the conductors cannot easily change their position. After this it 
shall not be possible to push the cord further into the fan. 

The flexible cord shall then be subjected 100 times to a pull of 10 kg for 
one second* Immediately afterwards, the cord shall be subjected to a torque 
of 3-5 kg/cm for a period of one minute. The test shall be made with the 
flexible cord suitable for the fan and conforming to IS : 434 (Part I) - 
1964* and IS : 434 (Part II) - 1964t or IS : 694 (Part I) - 1964$ and 

■^Specification £br rubber-imulated cabl^: Part I With copper conductors (fwistd). 
tSpectfication for rubber-ioiukted cables: Part II With alumltdum oonducton {misid). 
iSpedfication tor PVG insulated cables (for voltages up to 1 100 V): Part I With copper 
cMkductOft {mittd).

IS : 694 (Part II) . 1964*. During the test, no damage shall be caused 
to the flexible cord. 

At the end of the test the cord shall not have been displaced by more 
than 2 mm and the ends of the conductors shall not have been noticeably 
displaced in the terminals. 

18.7 Mechanical Endurance Test (for Regulators Only) (Type 
Test) — The regulator shall continue to function satisfactorily after being 
subjected to a test of 2500 operations of the regulator switch v^hen connected 
to a fan with locked rotor or an electrical load of equivalent impedance 
supplied at the maximum rated voltage. One operation includes a full 
cycle of movement from the *Off' position to the Tull Speed' position (or to 
the other extreme position) and back to 'GIT'. The test shall be made 
approximately at the rate of 6 operations per minute. 

18.8 Power Factor Test (for ac Fans Only) (Type Test) — The power 
factor of the fan with its Associated capacitor, if any, in circuit when tested 
at the test voltage and the highest speed of the fan shall be not less than 0-90. 

18.9 ac Leakage Test (Type Test) — The fan shall be made to rest on 
a base well insulated from the earth and single-pole change-over switch^ shall 
be arranged as shown in Fig. 5 to connect a multi-range milliammeter 
between frame and each live part of the fan in turn. 

Note 1 — To avoid risk to the milliammeter a suitable high resistance with a shunting 
switch may be used in series with the meter. 1 he shunting switch should be kept open 
to start with and when it is ensured that the meter is safe in both the positions of the 
change-over switch, the shunting switch shall be closed and readings taken. 

Note 2 — If interference suppression devices are fitted to the fan they shall he dis* 
connected during the test.

Leakage Current

18.9.1 The resistance of the measuring circuit shall be 2 000 ±100 
ohms. 

18.9. 1.1 Care shall be taken that normal earthing connections arc not 
made. It is recommended that the fan should be supplied through an 
isolating transformer; otherwise the fan shall be insulated from earth. 

18.9.1.2 The test shall be made with ac except in the case of fans for 
dc only, when dc is used. 

18.9.1.3 The milliammetcr used to measure the leakage current should 
have an impedance small in comparison with that of the circuit under test 
and be of a type not appreciably affected by current wave-forms. 

18.9.2 A voltage M times the rated voltage or to M times the upper 
limit of the rated voltage range shall be supplied to the fan; and it is operated 
as in normal use for a period of at least 10 minutes. The leakage current 
which may flow from any pole of the supply mains to the accessible metal 
parts and metal foil on external parts of insulating material, connected 
together, shall be measured under operating conditions. 

18.9.2.1 The leakage current shall be measured with the milliammeter 
connected alternatively to lines 1 and 2. 

18.9.3 The leakage current for either of the positions {see 18.9.2.1) shall 
not exceed 300 ftA (peak). 

18.10 High Voltage Test (Acceptance Test) 

18.10.1 The source of supply for the high voltage test shall be not less 
than 500 VA. 

18.10.2 The high voltage test shall be applied to all new and completed 
fan motors and regulators in normal working conditions with all parts in 
place except the capacitors which should be disconnected. 

18.10.3 An ac test voltage at any convenient frequency between 40 and 
60 c/s of approximately sine wave-form shall be applied and maintained for 
one minute without showing any kind of breakdown or flashovcr. 

The test voltage shall be applied as follows : 
a) For fan motors 

1) Between live parts and other inaccessible metal 1 500 volts 

parts (that is^ over the functional insulation) 
m the case of double insulated motors 

2) Between the inaccessible metal parts and the 2 500 volts 

body (that is, over the supplementary insula- 
tion) in the case of double insulated motors 

3) Between live parts and body (that is, over the 4 000 volts 

reinforced insulation) for reinforced insulated 
motors 

22 



IS : 4327-1967 

b) For regulators 

1) Between any terminal and the body 1 500 volts 

2) Between the terminals with the regulator in the 1 500 volts 

*Off' position 

18.10.4 At the end of one minute, the test voltage shall be removed and 
the insulation-resistance test conducted as in 18,11. 

18.11 Iiisiilatioii-Redistance Test (Acceptance Test) 

18.11.1 The insulation-resistance test shall be carried out on fans and 
regulators immediately after conducting the flash test {see 18.15). 

Note — When conducted as a type test for fans and regulators, this test shall follow the 
xnoistureproofness test {su 18.5). 

18.11.2 The insulation-resistance of the fan motor and its regulator shall 
be not less than two megohms when tested after the completion of the high 
voltage test, with a dc voltage of approximately 500 volts applied between 
points used for the high voljagc test or flash test. 

18.12 EartUag Continiiity Test (Acceptance Test) - For fans intended 
to be earthed, the resistance when measured witli a current of 10 amperes 
with a dc voltage not exceeding 6 volts, shall not exceed 0- 1 ohm between 
any exposed metal parts except the rotating parts supported by meftal 
bearings, and: 

a) the free end of the earthing conductor if the fan is fitted with a 
flexible cord, due allowance being made for the resistance of #ie 
earthing conductor of the flexible cord; or 

b) the earthing terminal or contact, where the fan is supplied without 
a flexible cord. 

UJ3 Electrical Input Test (Acceptance Test) 

18.13*! The electrical power input of ceiling type fans shall be determinet! 
by running the fan at the test voltage as specified in 18.1.3 with the regulator 
(if any) at the highest speed position. 

18«13«2 The electrical power input of a cabin type fan shall be determined 
by running the fan with the axis of the blades horizontal at the test voltage 
specified with the regulator (if any) in the highest speed position and with 
the oscillating mechanism (if any) connected. 

The oscillating mechanism, if any, shall then be disconnected and the 
position of the fan fixed so that the direction of the axis of the draught (that 
18, the axis of the rotation of the fan blades) is perpendicular to the test plane. 
The fan shall then be restarted with the test voltage applied to the terminals 
and the electrical input in watts again measured. The diflerence between 
this and the first reading shall be taken as the power absorbed by the 
oscillating mechanism. 

23 



IS : 4327-1967 

18.14 Measttrement of Fan Speed (Acceptance Test) — The speed of 
rotation of the fan shall be determined by running the fan at the test voltage 
and at its rated frequency (if ac). The method of measurement shall be 
jfuch that the speed of the fan is not appreciably affected. 

18.15 Flash Test (Routine Test) — Every fan and regulator shall with- 
stand the voltage specified in 18.10.3 for one second when it is applied 
instantaneously.

20. TOLERANCES ON RATINGS 

20.1 For a fan covered by this standard, in no case shall the measured 
performance be inferior to that given in this standard. 

20.2 In addition, the observed test results expressed as a percentage of 
the rating assigned by the manufacturer {see 2.3) shall be within the foUqwing 
limits: 

Air delivery Not less than 90 percent 

Service value Not less than 90 percent 



APPENDIX A 

{Clause 17.3) 

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION TO BE SUPPLIED BY THE 
MANUFACTURER 

A»l. The following additional information in respect of a fan shall be supplied 
by the manufacturer on request : 

a) Power factor (if ac), 

b) Rated speed in rev/min, 

c) Air delivery at test voltage, 

d) Service value at rated voltage, 
c) Number and type of blades, 

f ) Type of regulator and number of running positions, 

g) Class of insulation, 

h) Type of bearings, and 

j) Instructions for lubrication of bearings.

B.2. CaUTERU FOR CONFORMITY 

B-2.1 If no defectives arc found in the first sample (col 2 of Tabic 4), accept 
the lot. If the number of defectives found is greater than or equal to the 
rejection number (col 4 of Table 4), reject the lot. If the number of 
defectives found in the first sample is less than the rejection number, tajte a 
second sample of size indicated in col 3 of Table 4 and if the total number 
of defectives in the first and second samples put together is less than the 
rejection number, accept the lot; otherwise not.

* Note — The need for specifying litniu of noise levels ( acoustical ) of the fans b
